title: DC-ViT: Modulating Spatial and Channel Interactions for Multi-Channel Images
claim: Keeping per-channel processing separate before introducing cross-channel interaction yields consistent gains over unified-attention baselines across several backbones.
layout: 2 panels, bar chart left, pipeline diagram right, color-coded stage labels
description: The left panel is a grouped bar chart of average score (y-axis 50–75) for three multi-channel ViT backbones: ChannelViT, DiChaViT and ChaMAEViT. Each backbone has a blue MC-ViT baseline bar and a taller orange '+ DC-ViT' bar. The right panel is a left-to-right architecture schematic. Stacked microscopy channel images x0, x1, ..., xc (blue, yellow and red stains) enter a grey rounded box through a trapezoid 'tokeniser'. They then pass through a row of vertical blocks: blue DSA(sp) blocks for l∉M, red DSA(sp+ch) blocks for l∈M, and a final blue DSA(sp) block. A green trapezoid 'DAG' aggregates the channels into an output embedding z∈R^D. Curly braces and arrows in blue and red link the block colors to the l∉M and l∈M conditions. Blue and red labels under the boxes name the stages: independent feature learning, cross-channel interactions and channel-conditioned learning.
caption: Schematic of DC-ViT. Channels build strong lowlevel representations independently, and are then introduced to cross-channel interactions. DSA(sp) and DSA(sp+ch) denote DC-ViT blocks (Eq. 1) with l /∈M and l ∈M in Eq. 2, respectively.
abstract: Training and evaluation in multi-channel imaging (MCI) remains challenging due to heterogeneous channel configurations arising from varying staining protocols, sensor types, and acquisition settings. This heterogeneity limits the applicability of fixed-channel encoders commonly used in general computer vision. Recent Multi-Channel Vision Transformers (MC-ViTs) address this by enabling flexible channel inputs, typically by jointly encoding patch tokens from all channels within a unified attention space. However, unrestricted token interactions across channels can lead to feature dilution, reducing the ability to preserve channel-specific semantics that are critical in MCI data. To address this, we propose Decoupled Vision Transformer (DC-ViT), which explicitly regulates information sharing using Decoupled Self-Attention (DSA), which decomposes token updates into two complementary pathways: spatial updates that model intra-channel structure, and channel-wise updates that adaptively integrate cross-channel information. This decoupling mitigates informational collapse while allowing selective inter-channel interaction. To further exploit these enhanced channel-specific representations, we introduce Decoupled Aggregation (DAG), which allows the model to learn task-specific channel importances. Extensive experiments across three MCI benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing MC-ViT approaches. Code is available at https://github.com/umarikkar/DCViT.
